answer: Sybil resistance can come from bonded vouching: a new agent becomes a vertex in the trust graph only when an existing agent stakes escrowed funds on it for 30 days. If the newcomer cheats, the voucher's stake is slashed and the voucher's own vertex loses weight. A fake cluster must therefore lock real capital per identity, and one flagged identity burns its sponsors. Auditors publish a periodic beacon of random checks, so no sybil can predict which tasks get verified, and no harbor of idle fakes stays cheap.
